summary: Air-gapped installer preflight fails: "unknown signing key" after Redwood signing key rotation (trust store not updated)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports Redwood Private on-prem installer blocks upgrade due to signature verification failure: "Unknown signing key" / "untrusted key id".
- Triggered immediately after Redwood signing key rotation for offline bundle releases.

Customer / Impact
- Customer: GovLab Research (Private, air-gapped environment)
- Impact: Upgrade blocked in preflight; customer cannot proceed with planned maintenance window. No production outage yet, but upgrade window at risk.

Environment
- Deployment: Redwood Private (on-prem), air-gapped
- Installer: redwood-private-installer v1.12.3 (customer-reported)
- Bundle: redwood-private-offline-bundle 2026.01.0 (customer-reported)
- Transport: bundle moved via offline media (external drive)

What happened
- Redwood rotated the offline bundle signing key as part of scheduled rotation.
- Customer environment has a pinned trust store containing the previous Redwood public signing key only.
- New bundles are signed with the new key; the installer correctly fails closed when the signer key is not in the local trust store.

Error (customer-provided)
- Preflight output:
  - "Signature verification failed: UNTRUSTED_SIGNING_KEY"
  - "Key ID: redwood-release-signing-2026q1 not found in trust store"
  - "Install blocked. Update trust roots or contact Support."

Repro steps (support)
1) In an environment with an outdated trust store (previous key only), run:
   - redwood-private-installer preflight --bundle /mnt/offline/redwood-private-2026.01.0.bundle
2) Observe failure during bundle verification with unknown/untrusted key.

Triage notes
- This matches expected behavior after key rotation; likely not a product defect.
- Need to confirm: (a) customer is on an installer version that supports trust store updates/rollover, (b) they received/used the updated trust roots package or docs step.

Requested outcome
- Provide customer with the updated Redwood public signing key (trust roots) and the documented update procedure for air-gapped environments.
- Confirm preflight succeeds after trust store update.
- Capture evidence for customer security review (key rotation notice + key fingerprint) if requested.
comments: 2026-01-16 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Opened ticket from customer email via Rachel Kim. Customer reports upgrade blocked with "unknown signing key" after pulling latest offline bundle. Asked for: installer version, exact command output, and whether they updated trust roots per key-rotation notice.

2026-01-16 (Rachel Kim, Customer Success) — GovLab confirms installer v1.12.3; they did not apply any separate trust-store update. They assumed the new bundle contained everything required. Maintenance window scheduled 2026-01-17 02:00 local.

2026-01-16 (Dev Patel, Support) — Confirmed expected behavior post-rotation. Action: provide trust store update steps + link to docs and offer a short call to walk through in air-gapped workflow. Also noted that break-glass flag exists but is policy-gated and should not be used as routine remediation.

2026-01-16 (Dev Patel, Support) — Sent customer the 'Key rotation & trust store updates' doc link and summarized steps:
1) Obtain updated Redwood signing public key bundle ("redwood-trust-roots" package) via approved transfer channel.
2) On the installer host, update trust store:
   - redwood-private-installer trust import --file /path/to/redwood-release-signing-2026q1.pub
   - OR replace trust store directory at /etc/redwood/trust-roots/ (per doc)
3) Re-run:
   - redwood-private-installer verify-bundle --bundle /mnt/offline/redwood-private-2026.01.0.bundle --verbose
4) Then re-run preflight.
Included the new key fingerprint and requested they validate it out-of-band with their security team.

2026-01-17 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Customer updated trust roots and re-ran verification successfully. They reported:
- "Bundle signature verification: OK"
- "Signer: redwood-release-signing-2026q1"
Proceeding with upgrade.

2026-01-17 (Dev Patel, Support) — Follow-up: advised customer to document trust-root update as a prerequisite step for future offline bundle upgrades, and to subscribe to Redwood Private release/security notices for rotations. Offered to provide a short security attestation statement describing rotation cadence and key custody if Procurement asks.

2026-01-18 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Internal note: this is the 3rd case this week; recommend adding a more explicit installer error message pointing users directly to the trust-store update doc and including the expected key ID + fingerprint. Consider proactive comms to Private air-gapped accounts before next rotation.
resolution: Root cause: Customer trust store contained only the previous Redwood offline bundle signing key; after scheduled key rotation the new offline bundle was signed by a new key that was not yet trusted locally. Resolution: Customer imported the updated Redwood public signing key into the installer trust store (air-gapped transfer), re-ran bundle verification successfully, and proceeded with upgrade. No break-glass override used.
